summary: Locking the garage mid-theft teleports the thief AND the stolen car out of the garage, facing the road. The victim's most obvious reaction to the alarm gives the thief a free escape.
evidence: PlotService.luau:1242-1251: pushOut finds a non-owner seated in a Vehicle-tagged car and calls carModel:PivotTo(spot * CFrame.new(0, ride+0.5, -2)). spot comes from _drivewayOffset (PlotService.luau:250-254), which is FRONT_Z-12, i.e. outside the door. plotToWorld keeps the plot orientation, so the car faces the entrance road. lockFor calls pushOut immediately (1309) and again every 0.5s (1616-1617). Nothing checks Kind=Stolen, TheftVictimUserId or TheftService. GarageClient.luau:647-700 shows a big red 'LOCK GARAGE' button to the owner whenever they are inside. pushOut uses a raw PivotTo, not VehicleService.teleport (VehicleService.luau:990-996, which resets the watchdog). For slower cars the jump of about 100 studs can trip watchdogPass (VehicleService.luau:1561-1575), which calls violate and rewinds the car into the garage (1527) for 2s before the next push. This was already listed as a known issue in docs/integration/economy-server.md:136 and :211 and never fixed.
failureScenario: A completes the hold on B's Epic and is seated inside B's garage. The siren starts and B, standing in the garage, taps LOCK GARAGE. On the next push tick A and the car are placed on the driveway facing the street. The gate now blocks B's own pursuit car only for non-owners, and A drives off. With a slow car, A's car may instead rubber-band back in, then out, for about 2s.
suggestedFix: In pushOut, when the seated car has Kind=='Stolen' and TheftVictimUserId == st.owner.UserId (or TheftService.getTheftForCar(car).victim == st.owner), call VehicleService.eject(car) and push only the character. The car then becomes 'dropped' inside the locked garage and B can Recover it, so locking works as a trap. For every other vehicle, use VehicleService.teleport(car, cf) instead of a raw PivotTo so the watchdog does not rewind it.
verifyReason: Confirmed. PlotService.pushOut (PlotService.luau ~1229-1266) checks only that the seat is a VehicleSeat in a model tagged Vehicle, then calls carModel:PivotTo(spot*CFrame.new(0,ride+0.5,-2)). spot = plotToWorld(_drivewayOffset(n)) with Z = FRONT_Z-12 = -56, so the car lands outside the gate facing the road. lockFor calls pushOut immediately and the start() loop calls it every 0.5s. Nothing in tryLock, lockFor or pushOut looks at Kind, TheftVictimUserId or TheftService. GarageClient.updateLockUI shows the LOCK button whenever the owner is inside (Visible = not driving and (inside or locked)). The watchdog rewind is possible but not certain. setDriver resets wdAt at seating, so a lock in the first ~0.5s, or while the car is moving (dt≈0.5, allowance cap*0.5+10 = 45-77 studs), against a jump from a back slot (~100 studs) trips 'teleport' and violate() pivots the car back for 2s. Both docs entries (economy-server.md:136, :211) are present and the issue was never fixed. Downgraded from high to medium: without the lock the thief only needs a few seconds to drive out. The real harm is that the owner's natural reaction removes their bonk chance and gives the thief a free exit, instead of trapping them.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau, pushOut: when carModel:GetAttribute('Kind') == 'Stolen' and carModel:GetAttribute('TheftVictimUserId') == st.owner.UserId (st.owner may be nil, so guard it), do `local VS = sys('VehicleService'); local car = VS and VS.fromModel(carModel); if car then VS.eject(car) end`, then re-read the root and push only the character, as in the on-foot branch. The car stays inside the locked garage as 'dropped' and the owner can Recover it. For every other seated vehicle, replace the raw PivotTo with `VS.teleport(car, cf)` so the watchdog does not rewind it, and keep the velocity zeroing. Optional, in src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau canTakeover: refuse ('🔒 Garage locked!') while PlotService.isLocked(victimPlot) and MapLayout.plotAt(carPosition(theft.car)) == victimPlot. This stops the pushed-out thief from re-hotwiring through the gate within prompt range, which would cause an eject/seat loop.

summary: An alt or a friend can farm the recovery and revenge bonuses, worth about 50s of the victim's total income every ~27s. The same loop lets anyone grief a victim with repeated alarms and paused income.
evidence: markDropped (TheftService.luau:868-877) accepts a voluntary hop-out with a 12s timer, and the RecoverPrompt (761-774) appears straight away. recover (1401-1429) pays _bonus(incomeOf(victim), RECOVERY_BONUS_SECONDS=30) whenever the slot is restored. The bonus is based on the victim's whole income, not the stolen car's, and there is no check that the car left the garage or that the thief was knocked out. onThiefHit (1466-1472) pays REVENGE_BONUS_SECONDS=20 once per theft, and revengePaid resets with each new theft. The cooldown is only THEFT_VICTIM_COOLDOWN=25s (Economy.luau:133; setCooldown 429-432, applied again in finish at 633). beginTheft also counts progress(thief,'steal',1) at the start (1199), so aborted thefts fill the 'Steal 5/12 cars' contracts.
failureScenario: B has 3 or more cars, including a Rustbucket. B's alt holds Steal on the Rustbucket (1.1s), hops out at once, and B bonks the alt and holds Recover (0.3s). B gets 50s of total income and repeats every ~27s, close to 3x income. Without an alt, any griefer can repeat start-and-abandon every 25s to set off B's red vignette and siren and pause that slot's income.
suggestedFix: Pay the recovery bonus only if the thief was knocked out by the victim (theft.lastHitBy == victim within KNOCKOUT_WINDOW) and the car was driven more than about 60 studs from the slot, or the theft lasted more than about 15s. Base it on the stolen car's income, not the total. Cap bonuses per (victim, thief) pair, for example once per 10 minutes. Count the 'steal' contract only on delivery. Give a player who abandons thefts repeatedly a longer personal cooldown, for example 60s on the same victim.
verifyReason: Confirmed. markDropped (TheftService.luau ~868) runs on any empty seat, including a voluntary exit (knocked=false gives the 12s THEFT_ABANDON_LIMIT), and addDropPrompts creates the victim's RecoverPrompt (RECOVER_HOLD 0.3s) straight away. recover() pays _bonus(incomeOf(victim), RECOVERY_BONUS_SECONDS=30). incomeOf is GarageService.incomePerSec, i.e. total income. There is no check on distance moved, theft duration, knock-out or who the thief was. onThiefHit pays REVENGE_BONUS_SECONDS=20 once per theft (revengePaid lives on the Theft record), and CombatService.shouldAddAssaultHeat gives the victim no heat for hitting someone stealing from them. Cooldown is only THEFT_VICTIM_COOLDOWN=25 (setCooldown in beginTheft and finish). A Common display car's hold is 0.8*1.4 = 1.12s. A cycle of about 27-28s therefore pays 50s of total income, roughly 2.8x effective income. Two friends can also alternate roles because the cooldown is per victim. The 'steal' contract counted at beginTheft matches how street steals count on hotwire, so that part is a minor side effect, not a separate bug.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: (1) Keep a ledger `bonusPaid[victimUserId][thiefUserId] = clock` and pay the recovery bonus (recover) and the active-theft revenge bonus (onThiefHit) at most once per (victim, thief) pair per ~600s, pruned in start() like recentRobbers. (2) In recover, pay the bonus only if the car left the victim's plot (MapLayout.plotAt(carPosition(car)) ~= plotIndexOf(victim)) or now - theft.startedAt >= ~15s. Otherwise just restore the slot with the '🏠 back home' notify. (3) Base the bonus on the stolen car's income: EconomyMath.carIncome(theft.carId, theft.mutation) * GarageService.multiplier(victim), not incomeOf(victim). Constants can go in src/shared/Config/Economy.luau. Update tests/spec/theft.spec.luau (the recover/revenge cases around lines 573-653).

summary: The victim's side of the chase is close to unwinnable, which goes against pillars 1, 3 and 5. There is no warning while the thief holds the prompt, no way to grab a car away from the garage, no bat button while driving, the stolen car keeps full speed, and a ramming wreck gives the victim nothing.
evidence: PromptButtonHoldBegan only records os.clock() (GarageService.luau:552-554); the owner is never told. DriveCar requires being inside your own garage or within 40 studs of the slot (GarageService.luau:908-913), and no client fires DriveCar remotely. CombatClient.refreshButtons hides ActionButton while driving (CombatClient.luau:616-626), so phones have no bat button in a car. The bat needs to be within BAT_RANGE 9 + slack (CombatService.luau:920-927). The Stolen car spawns with no SpeedMultiplier (TheftService.luau:1116-1122), so an Epic does about 110-135 studs/s while the victim's chase car may be a 70 studs/s Common. A ram that wrecks the stolen car goes to onDestroyed then failTheft('wrecked') (TheftService.luau:1502-1508), which pays the victim no recovery or revenge bonus even though car.data.lastDamagedBy is recorded (VehicleService.luau:1300-1302). The victim's banner shows no countdown of the thief's remaining time.
failureScenario: B is on the other side of the map when the alarm sounds. B cannot spawn a car, sees an Epic driving away at full speed, and on a phone could not swing the bat from a car even after catching up. The alarm only adds frustration.
suggestedFix: (1) Fire an 'INTRUDER: X is hotwiring your <car>!' Notify plus sound to the owner on StealPrompt HoldBegan, and highlight the lock button. (2) Give player-stolen cars a debuff, e.g. model SpeedMultiplier 0.85 (VehicleController already polls it) and no nitro. (3) Show the bat ActionButton while driving, or add a side-swipe 'BONK' button when within range of a Stolen car. (4) During an active theft, allow DriveCar from anywhere so the victim's car spawns on the nearest lane. (5) Treat a wreck caused by car.data.lastDamagedBy == victim as a recovery and pay the bonus. (6) Add the thief's endsAt to the CarStolenAlert banner.
verifyReason: Partly confirmed, headline overstated. Confirmed: GarageService's StealPrompt PromptButtonHoldBegan only records display.holds[p] (GarageService.luau ~552), so the owner gets no warning during holds of 1.1s (Common) up to 8.4s (Mythic), and the lock and pushOut can only be used pre-emptively. The CarStolenAlert banner has no countdown (NotificationController buildAlertUI shows only a title and a static subtitle). DriveCar needs the garage or 40 studs, and no client fires it. CombatClient.refreshButtons hides actionButton while driving. Stolen cars get no SpeedMultiplier (only PoliceService sets one). A wreck goes to onDestroyed then failTheft('wrecked') with no bonus. Refuted parts: the victim has real counterplay that the tracer ignored. The spike button is shown while driving (refreshButtons: show = driving and has spikes). Street and traffic cars can be hotwired to give chase. The taser has range 60. The thief gets police heat, a 150s limit, and can be hijacked. ManualActivationOnly=false means a tap can still activate an equipped bat on mobile. So this is not 'close to unwinnable', but the missing hold warning is a real gap against pillar 5.
fix: Minimal, high-value subset: (1) In src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau, in the StealPrompt PromptButtonHoldBegan handler, when the owner `player` is online, send a throttled (per thief, ~5s) Notify('warning', '🚨 '..thief.DisplayName..' is hotwiring your '..label..'! LOCK or BONK!') plus a Sound. Optionally GarageClient pulses the lock button. (2) In src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau, show the remaining time in the alert subtitle, read from the TheftEndsAt attribute of the Workspace.Vehicles model whose TheftVictimUserId == LocalPlayer.UserId. Speed debuffs, remote DriveCar and paying a bonus on a victim-caused wreck are balance choices. A wreck bonus should only ship together with F2's per-pair cap, or it becomes another farm.

summary: The '🔨 B knocked A out of B's <car>!' EventFeed line never fires on a normal knock-out, because the eject happens before onThiefHit records the hitter.
evidence: CombatService.applyHit stuns the victim (879), then ejects (880-881), and only then calls TheftService.onThiefHit (885). eject runs setDriver(nil), which fires DriverChanged. Signal:Fire runs handlers immediately through task.spawn (Signal.luau:48-56), so TheftService.onDriverChanged runs markDropped (TheftService.luau:1489-1497) before onThiefHit. In markDropped, `local hitter = theft.lastHitBy` is still nil (initialised at 1151), so the EventFeed block at 900-908 is skipped. The knocked flag only comes out right because the Stunned attribute is set first.
failureScenario: B bonks A out of B's Epic. The server never broadcasts a knock-out line, so one of the 'moments worth clipping' from pillar 3 is silently lost on every first hit.
suggestedFix: In applyHit, call TheftService.onThiefHit(attacker, victim) before VehicleService.eject (move line 885 above 880). Alternatively, have markDropped read the hitter from CombatService's last hit or task.defer the feed line.
verifyReason: Confirmed. In CombatService.applyHit (~877-885) the order is stun, then callSystem('VehicleService','eject',car), then callSystem('TheftService','onThiefHit',...). eject runs setDriver(car,nil) synchronously, which calls DriverChanged:Fire. Signal:Fire uses task.spawn, which runs the handler immediately, so TheftService.onDriverChanged runs markDropped before onThiefHit. markDropped does not yield before `local hitter = theft.lastHitBy`, which is still nil on the first hit (initialised nil in beginTheft and on takeover), so the EventFeed block is skipped. knocked is still correct because CombatService.stun sets the Stunned attribute first. The impact is cosmetic only (a missing feed line), so low.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau applyHit: move `callSystem("TheftService", "onThiefHit", attacker, victim)` to just before `if car then callSystem("VehicleService", "eject", car) end`. onThiefHit only sets lastHitAt and lastHitBy and pays revenge, so nothing in it depends on the eject. Add a theft.spec case that a hit followed by a drop fires the EventFeed.

summary: After a drop, the thief's HUD keeps showing 'DELIVER IT HOME! 1:42' while the car will actually be towed in 12-20s.
evidence: TheftService.sendThiefState sends dropped and droppedEndsAt (TheftService.luau:539-548). StateController.sanitizeTheft keeps only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot (StateController.luau:86-96). HUDController.applyTheft and refreshTheft (HUDController.luau:1303-1341) therefore always count down the 150s endsAt. The HUD integration doc already lists this as a deviation that was never applied.
failureScenario: A is bonked out and sees 1:30 left on the HUD, so does not hurry. 20s later the car disappears. The only hints were a 4-second toast and a waypoint label.
suggestedFix: Keep dropped and droppedEndsAt in sanitizeTheft. In the HUD, switch to a red 'GET BACK IN! 0:12' state using droppedEndsAt while dropped.
verifyReason: Confirmed. sendThiefState sends dropped and droppedEndsAt (TheftService.luau ~539-548), but StateController.sanitizeTheft (~86-96) keeps only active, endsAt, carId and targetPlot, and the TheftState type has no dropped field. HUDController.applyTheft and refreshTheft always count down the 150s endsAt. This is listed as a deviation in gameplay-client.md:334. Downgraded to low because the thief does get a 4s toast with the real tow time and the waypoint label switches to 'GET BACK IN!'.
fix: src/client/Controllers/StateController.luau: add `dropped = raw.dropped == true` and `droppedEndsAt = num-or-nil(raw.droppedEndsAt)` to sanitizeTheft and to the TheftState type. src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau: in applyTheft store the dropped state; in refreshTheft, while dropped, use droppedEndsAt with the label/colour 'GET BACK IN! 0:12' (Danger) instead of endsAt. Extend the clientcore.spec sanitizeTheft case.

summary: A victim can always cancel a theft by leaving (and rejoin to get the car back with offline earnings). The car disappears from under the thief with no compensation, and the thief keeps the wanted star.
evidence: onPlayerRemoving (TheftService.luau:1575-1584) and the tick (1527-1529) call failTheft(theft,'victim_left'). This destroys the car (645-647) and skips the restore (649-651); the thief only gets the toast '😶 X left. The {car} vanished!' (_failText 387-388). DataService.release fires Releasing (DataService.luau:1079) before the final writeAsync (1082), so a transfer could be hooked in at that point.
failureScenario: A has driven B's Mythic most of the way home. B leaves the game, A's car vanishes mid-drive, A keeps +1 star and cops, and gets nothing. B rejoins with the Mythic. This contradicts 'fair theft' and makes stealing from experienced players pointless.
suggestedFix: Hook DataService.Releasing. If the theft has run more than N seconds, or the thief is outside the victim's garage, remove the record from the victim's data before the final save and give it to the thief (storeCar or a pending queue), with the usual uncollected payout. At minimum, pay the thief chopValue and clear their wanted level.
verifyReason: Confirmed. onPlayerRemoving and _tick call failTheft(theft,'victim_left'), which destroys the car and skips restoreVictimSlot. The record never left the victim's data, and the thief only gets '😶 X left. The {car} vanished!' while keeping the theft heat. However, this is spec-sanctioned: SPEC §6 TheftService says fail is 'Triggered by: time limit, victim leaving (car vanishes, thief notified)', which is consistent with pillar 5 ('Offline garages can't be robbed'). The victim also pays a real cost (leaving the server and plot). So this is a design trade-off, not a bug. Moving the car on DataService.Releasing is risky: it adds a data-ordering dependency and gives alts a way to transfer cars instantly without delivering.
fix: If the team wants to change it, first update docs/SPEC.md §6 TheftService. Then the minimal change in src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau failTheft for reason 'victim_left': if online(thief) and the car is outside the victim's plot, or hooks.clock() - theft.startedAt >= ~30s, pay the thief a consolation (e.g. EconomyMath.chopValue(carId, mutation), capped) through DataService.addCash, and call WantedService to remove the playerTheft heat added for this theft. Do not move the car record on Releasing.

summary: The Steal prompt is shown, and the full hold is required, even when the server will refuse: victim on cooldown, victim already being robbed, or the thief's garage is full.
evidence: GarageClient.updatePrompts enables Steal based only on mine, driving, locked and CarCount (GarageClient.luau:135-139). The refusals with codes victimBusy, cooldown and full (TheftService.luau:342-350) only run after the hold, from steal.Triggered then beginTheft (GarageService.luau:555-576). There is no replicated cooldown or busy attribute on the plot, and the thief's own free-slot count from the snapshot is not checked.
failureScenario: Right after C robbed B, A holds E for 3.5s on B's Epic and gets '⏳ They were just robbed — try again in 12s'. With a full garage, A holds 3.5s and gets 'Your garage is full!'. The player could not have known in advance.
suggestedFix: Server: set plot attributes RobbableAt (cooldown end, server time) and BeingRobbed. Client: disable the Steal prompt or set its ObjectText to 'PROTECTED 0:12' / 'BEING ROBBED' / 'YOUR GARAGE IS FULL', using those attributes and the local snapshot's free slots.
verifyReason: Confirmed. GarageClient.updatePrompts enables Steal on `not mine and not driving and not locked and cars >= NEWBIE_PROTECTION_CARS` only. victimBusy, cooldown and full are only checked server-side in _canSteal after the hold completes (steal.Triggered then beginTheft). The cooldown is not replicated anywhere. 'Busy' could be derived from the existing pad State='BeingStolen' attributes, but the client does not do this. The thief's free slots are in the local snapshot but are not checked. The cost is a wasted hold (1.1s up to 8.4s) followed by a clear error toast, so this is UX, low severity.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: in setCooldown, also set a plot attribute `RobbableAt` = toServerTime(cooldownUntil) on PlotService.getPlotModel(plotIndexOf(victim)). src/client/Controllers/GarageClient.luau updatePrompts: also disable Steal when any pad in view.model has State == 'BeingStolen', when Workspace:GetServerTimeNow() < RobbableAt, or when StateController's snapshot shows no free slots. Re-run updatePlotPrompts on a short timer or attribute change so the prompt re-enables when RobbableAt passes.

summary: The daily contract 'Bonk 3 thieves out of cars' only counts when the attacker is the victim of that exact theft. Players need to be robbed 3 times in one UTC day and catch each thief, so the contract is effectively uncompletable.
evidence: CombatService.luau:869-870 sets `defended = car ~= nil and car.kind == 'Stolen' and stealingFromAttacker`, and progress('defend') only runs when defended is true (886-889). Economy.luau:177 defines { id='bonk3', text='Bonk 3 thieves out of cars', stat='defend', goal=3 }. A bystander (C) bonking a thief (A) does not count.
failureScenario: A player rolls bonk3 and spends the day hunting thieves. Bonking other players' thieves does not count, so the contract never progresses, which hurts the daily-contract retention pillar.
suggestedFix: Count any hit that ejects the driver of a Stolen car (or of a Loot car whose driver has Wanted ≥ 1). Keep the extra 'THIEF BONKED' message for the victim.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CombatService.applyHit sets `defended = car ~= nil and car.kind == 'Stolen' and stealingFromAttacker`, and isStealingFrom requires theft.victim == attacker. 'defend' is the only source of that stat (grep finds just CombatService.luau:887). The code matches SPEC §6 CombatService line 180 ('contract defend if that ejected a thief driving the attacker's stolen car'), so the defect is in the contract design. 'Bonk 3 thieves out of cars' needs the player to be robbed 3 times in one UTC day and to catch each thief while still seated. Players under 3 cars can never be robbed. The contract is therefore dead whenever it is rolled, and there is no reroll.
fix: src/server/Systems/CombatService.luau applyHit: compute `thiefEjected = car ~= nil and (car.kind == 'Stolen' or (car.kind == 'Loot' and (tonumber(victim:GetAttribute('Wanted')) or 0) >= 1))` and call RewardsService.progress(attacker,'defend',1) when thiefEjected. Keep the 'THIEF BONKED! Go grab your car back!' notify only when `defended`. Update docs/SPEC.md line 180 to match. Stun immunity (immuneUntil) already limits repeat-bonk farming of the same target.

summary: beginTheft and takeover treat 'seat() did not throw' as success. VehicleService.seat returns (false, reason) and never throws, so a failed seating starts or 'resumes' a theft with nobody in the car.
evidence: call() returns (pcallOk, firstResult) (TheftService.luau:160-172). beginTheft uses `local seatOk = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` (1190), which is true whenever the pcall succeeds. takeover's `local seatOk, err = call(...)` (971-974) only warns when the pcall fails. VehicleService.seat returns false with 'no character', 'occupied' or 'sit failed' (VehicleService.luau:908-918, 949-956) without throwing.
failureScenario: A's character dies or resets the moment the hold completes. The theft starts anyway: the slot shows STOLEN, A gets +1 star, B's alarm fires, and after 2s B gets 'Your car was dropped! Grab it back in 12s!'. On takeover, C sees 'GO GO GO!' and the drop prompts are cleared even if C was not seated, until the next tick drops the car again.
suggestedFix: Use `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)` and, if seated ~= true, run failTheft(theft,'error') (in beginTheft) or keep the car dropped and skip clearDropped (in takeover).
verifyReason: Confirmed. call() returns (pcallOk, result). beginTheft does `local seatOk = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief)`, which captures only pcallOk. takeover only warns when the pcall fails. VehicleService.seat returns (false, 'gone' | 'player' | 'not allowed' | 'no character' | 'occupied' | 'sit failed') and never throws. This is already documented in vehicles-world.md:311. The impact is limited. gatherState checked that the thief is alive moments before, with no realistic yield in between (spawn is synchronous), so a seat failure is rare. If it happens, the _tick safety net marks the car dropped after SEAT_GRACE. The visible symptom is a theft that started with nobody in the car (alarm, heat, 'dropped' toast).
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau beginTheft: `local okCall, seated = call('VehicleService','seat',car,thief); if not okCall or seated ~= true then failTheft(theft,'error') ... return false end` (the existing failure branch). In takeover, seat before clearing the drop state: if driverOf(car) ~= player, call seat; if it does not return true, notify the player 'Try again!' and return false without calling clearDropped (the prompts stay up). Otherwise clearDropped and continue.

summary: The free slot is checked only when the theft starts, not reserved. If it is filled during the theft (claiming a Playtime or Daily car from the menu while driving, or an owed Diamond Dragster being auto-delivered), delivery is refused and the thief has no way to sell from the car.
evidence: complete() refuses when freeSlots <= 0 (TheftService.luau:1248-1255) and the delivery is simply retried every 3s. storeCar uses the first free slot (GarageService.luau:745-747), so reward grants take the slot. The SellCar and DriveCar remotes exist (GarageService.luau:1296-1307), but no client code fires them; the only client-fired garage remote is LockGarage (GarageClient.luau:659). Selling therefore needs the on-foot SellPrompt, which means leaving the car, starting the 12s abandon timer and giving the victim a Recover prompt.
failureScenario: A, with 1 free slot, claims the 15-minute Rare gift while driving B's Epic and then reaches the drop-off. A sees 'Garage full! Sell a car to park this one. Hurry!', has to jump out and run to a display car, and B recovers the Epic.
suggestedFix: Reserve the slot at beginTheft (GarageService.reserveSlot or a pending marker that _firstFreeSlot respects), or let complete() overflow into a pending queue the way exclusives already work. Alternatively, have RewardsService and MonetizationService send cars to pending while the player has an active theft.
verifyReason: Confirmed but mostly self-inflicted. complete() refuses when freeSlots <= 0 and only notifies (throttled to 3s). storeCar takes the first free slot. No client fires SellCar or DriveCar (the client remotes are BuyTool, BuyUpgrade, ClaimDaily, ClaimPlaytime, GoHome, LockGarage, Rebirth, RedeemCode, SetSetting, ToolAction, TutorialDone, UnlockSlot), so selling needs the on-foot SellPrompt. The paths that fill a slot mid-theft are a player-initiated ClaimPlaytime or ClaimDaily car, or MonetizationService's periodic deliverExclusives loop. The latter only matters if the thief sold a car and started a theft before the next exclusive check. In the thief's own garage, hopping out to sell gives a 12s window, and the victim would need to be at the thief's garage to Recover, so the claimed loss is unlikely.
fix: Cheapest: in src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau (car grants) and src/server/Systems/MonetizationService.luau deliverExclusives, skip or defer car grants while TheftService.getActiveTheft(player) ~= nil and GarageService.freeSlots(player) <= 1. Rewards should stay claimable later, or fall back to the existing owed/cash fallback. Alternatively, let TheftService.complete treat a full garage like exclusives: remove the record from the victim and queue it as owed for the thief.

summary: The transfer is atomic in memory but saved as two separate, unordered DataStore writes. A hard server crash between them can duplicate the car (thief saved, victim not) or lose it.
evidence: TheftService.luau:1329-1336 starts saveNow(thief) and saveNow(victim) in two independent task.spawn calls. saveNow → writeAsync (DataService.luau:1034-1040) waits out the ~6s per-key cooldown independently for each key. BindToClose covers a graceful shutdown but not a crash.
failureScenario: The victim autosaved 2s ago, so their write waits about 4s, while the thief's write lands at once. The server crashes in that window, and both players load with the same car.
suggestedFix: Save sequentially in one task, victim first (removal), then thief. Better: stamp a transferId in both profiles and reconcile on load (if the victim still holds a record whose transferId the thief has, drop it).
verifyReason: Confirmed in principle. complete() starts saveNow(thief) and saveNow(victim) in two independent hooks.spawnTask calls. Each writeAsync respects its own per-key write rate, so the order is not defined. A hard server crash between the two writes can duplicate the car (thief saved, victim not) or lose it. BindToClose covers a graceful shutdown, and a player cannot trigger a crash on purpose, so this is a rare edge case. Low.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau complete(): replace the two spawns with one `hooks.spawnTask(function() pcall(DS.saveNow, victim); pcall(DS.saveNow, thief) end)`. Saving the removal first means a crash can at worst lose the car rather than duplicate it, which matters more for the economy. A transferId reconcile-on-load is optional hardening in DataService.luau.

summary: Wreck, bust and thief-leave all eject before the theft is failed, so the victim is first told the car was 'dropped, grab it in 20s' and then something different. Recover and Hotwire prompts are also put back onto a wrecked car, and recovering it pays the bonus.
evidence: VehicleService.wreck disables every prompt (VehicleService.luau:1319-1323) and then calls eject (1325). DriverChanged runs markDropped, which adds fresh, enabled drop prompts (TheftService.luau:882) and notifies the victim (887-895). The car is destroyed 2s later (1355-1357). The RecoverPrompt handler (TheftService.luau:761-774) does not check car.wrecked. WantedService.handleCar ejects (WantedService.luau:413) before TheftService.fail (417). VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving clears the driver (VehicleService.luau:1684-1688; connected in init before TheftService's handler at TheftService.luau:1618).
failureScenario: A crashes the Epic hard. B gets 'Your car was dropped! Grab it back in 20s!', runs over within 2s, holds Recover on the burning wreck and gets 'RECOVERED! +bonus' instead of 'wrecked... towed home'. When A is busted, B gets two contradictory toasts at once.
suggestedFix: In onDriverChanged, skip markDropped if car.wrecked or car.destroyed, or if the old driver is no longer online. Check car.wrecked in the RecoverPrompt handler. In WantedService.handleCar, call TheftService.fail before VehicleService.eject.
verifyReason: Confirmed. VehicleService.wreck disables prompts and then calls eject, which runs setDriver(nil) and DriverChanged (synchronous via task.spawn), and onDriverChanged runs markDropped. markDropped creates fresh, enabled Recover and Hotwire prompts and sends the victim 'dropped! Grab it back in 12s'. The car is destroyed WRECK_DESTROY_AFTER=2s later, then onDestroyed calls failTheft('wrecked'). The RecoverPrompt handler does not check car.wrecked, so a victim within reach during those 2s gets the full bonus. The Hotwire prompt shows but is a no-op, because addStealPrompt's Triggered checks car.wrecked. _tick would also call markDropped on a wrecked car. WantedService.handleCar ejects (~413) before TheftService.fail (~417), so the victim gets two contradictory toasts. For thief_left, VehicleService.onPlayerRemoving clears the driver, and during PlayerRemoving the player is still parented to Players, so markDropped treats them as online. Whether the toast appears depends on handler order. All of these are cosmetic or minor.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau: at the top of markDropped add `local c = theft.car; if type(c) == 'table' and (c.wrecked or c.destroyed) then return end` (this covers both the signal and the _tick path). In the RecoverPrompt Triggered handler, return early if car.wrecked or car.destroyed. src/server/Systems/WantedService.luau handleCar: for car.kind == 'Stolen', call TheftService.fail(car,'busted') before VehicleService.eject (fail destroys and ejects anyway). For thief_left, optionally defer markDropped in onDriverChanged (task.defer, then re-check theft.finished) so the PlayerRemoving fail wins.

summary: The victim's live 'YOUR CAR' arrow finds the thief by name, and the payload is a DisplayName. Duplicate DisplayNames, or another player's username matching it, make the arrow point at the wrong player.
evidence: TheftService sends CarStolenAlert(victim, nameOf(thief), ...) where nameOf returns the DisplayName (TheftService.luau:247-252, 1202). findPlayerByName (NotificationController.luau:1201-1213) first compares p.Name == name, then DisplayName. thiefPosition (1216-1242) tracks the matched player's seat or root. The car already carries TheftVictimUserId (TheftService.luau:1180).
failureScenario: There are two players with the DisplayName 'Alex' (common), or the thief's DisplayName equals another player's username. B's arrow leads to the wrong person while the real thief escapes.
suggestedFix: Track the car itself: on the client, find the model in Workspace.Vehicles whose TheftVictimUserId == LocalPlayer.UserId and TheftActive == true, and pass it to WaypointController.track. This also follows dropped cars and hijacks. Alternatively, add thiefUserId and VehicleId to the CarStolenAlert payload.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CarStolenAlert carries nameOf(thief), which is the DisplayName. NotificationController.findPlayerByName first matches p.Name == name and then the first p.DisplayName == name. thiefPosition follows that player's seat or root (and alertLastCar). Duplicate DisplayNames, or a username equal to the thief's DisplayName, point the arrow at the wrong player. This is rare in an 8-player server. The car already carries TheftVictimUserId, TheftThiefUserId and TheftActive attributes.
fix: src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau thiefPosition: first look in Workspace.Vehicles for a Model with TheftActive == true and TheftVictimUserId == Players.LocalPlayer.UserId and return its pivot. This also covers dropped and hijacked cars. Keep the name lookup only as a fallback. No server change is needed.

summary: A 15s re-arm against locks of 45-120s (+10s per rebirth) lets an AFK owner with a tap macro keep the garage locked 75-90% of the time. Together with offline protection, wealthy players become nearly unrobbable and the theft content dries up.
evidence: PlotService.LOCK_REARM = 15 (PlotService.luau:38), applied in unlock (1269-1281). tryLock only requires being inside the garage and the lock being ready (1331-1358). Lock values are { 45, 60, 90, 120 } in Economy.Upgrades.lock, plus 10s per rebirth (_lockDuration 245-247). The LockGarage remote allows 2 per second (1568-1570).
failureScenario: A level-3 lock owner AFKs in the garage with an autoclicker on 'LOCK GARAGE'. Thieves get a 15s window every 135s and must also cover the hold time and the walk in.
suggestedFix: Make the re-arm proportional (e.g. equal to the lock duration, for at most 50% uptime). Alternatively, give a fixed number of charges per 10 minutes, or require no lock while the owner has been idle for 2+ minutes.
verifyReason: Confirmed arithmetic. LOCK_REARM = 15 against lock values {45,60,90,120} + 10/rebirth gives 75% to 89%+ uptime for an owner who re-presses at once. The LockGarage remote allows 2/s, and the LockButton pad also locks on Touched, so idle-animation touches from an AFK owner standing on the pad may re-lock without a macro. The re-arm was added on purpose (economy-server.md:117), and a guaranteed 15s window plus the theft hold is a tuning choice. High lock uptime is common in the genre. This is a balance issue, not a defect.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau: make the re-arm proportional, e.g. `st.lockReadyAt = os.clock() + math.max(PlotService.LOCK_REARM, 0.5 * lastDuration)` (store the duration in lockFor or tryLock) and mirror it in the LockReadyAt attribute. Optionally ignore Touched-based tryLock unless the owner's Humanoid.MoveDirection was non-zero recently. Leave the Lockdown product (lockFor) bypass as it is.

summary: The revenge bonus for a completed robbery is skipped if the robber is currently stealing someone else's car.
evidence: onThiefHit (TheftService.luau:1465-1474) returns early whenever byThief[target] exists, even when the attacker is not that theft's victim. The recentRobbers check (1475-1482) is never reached, and the entry is not consumed.
failureScenario: A robbed B 2 minutes ago. B finds A stealing C's car and bonks A. B gets no 'REVENGE!' bonus, at exactly the dramatic moment the feature is meant for.
suggestedFix: Inside the active-theft branch, only return after handling that theft's victim case. Otherwise fall through to the recentRobbers check.
verifyReason: Confirmed. In onThiefHit, `local theft = byThief[target]; if theft and not theft.finished then ... return end` returns even when the attacker is not that theft's victim, so the recentRobbers branch is skipped. The entry is not consumed, though, so B still gets revenge with a later hit within REVENGE_WINDOW (300s) once A's current theft ends. The bonus is delayed or missed at the dramatic moment, not lost for good.
fix: src/server/Systems/TheftService.luau onThiefHit: inside the active-theft branch, after updating lastHitAt and lastHitBy, return only if the attacker == theft.victim case was handled, i.e. `if attacker == theft.victim then if not theft.revengePaid then ... end return end`. Otherwise fall through to the recentRobbers check. Add a theft.spec case: A robbed B, then A is stealing from C, then B bonks A and gets paid once.

summary: The CarStolenAlert banner (y=84, 92 tall) sits on the same top-centre strip as EventsClient's pill row (y=78) and the Hot Drop banner, so during a Hot Drop or Rush Hour the victim's alarm text is covered or covers them.
evidence: NotificationController.luau:58 ALERT_BANNER_POSITION = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 84); 1306-1313 Size 660x92 in HC_Banners. EventsClient.luau:184 places the pill row at UDim2.new(0.5,0,0,78). The HUD integration doc says the Hot Drop banner uses y=128-246.
failureScenario: A theft starts during a Hot Drop countdown. The red alarm banner and the Hot Drop banner overlap, and the theft text is unreadable on phones.
suggestedFix: Move the theft banner below the event strip (e.g. y=250), or hide or shift the EventsHUD while NotificationController.isAlertActive() is true.
verifyReason: Overlap confirmed, but the effect is the reverse of the claim. Both ScreenGuis use Kit.screen (IgnoreGuiInset=false, same UIScale). The theft banner is 660x92 at y=84 (84-176) in HC_Banners, and EventsHUD's Top frame is at y=78 with the pill row at 78-118 and the Hot Drop banner at 128-246. HC_Banners has DisplayOrder Theme.Layers.Banners=30 and EventsHUD has HUD+1=11, so the theft alarm draws on top and stays readable. What gets covered is the event pills and the top of the Hot Drop banner (title and timer) while a theft alert is active.
fix: src/client/Controllers/EventsClient.luau: while NotificationController.isAlertActive() is true (lazy require, checked in the existing render or update loop), offset the 'Top' frame down by ~104 design px (to y≈182), and restore it when the alert ends. Alternatively hide the pill row during the alert. Do not move the theft banner lower, because the centre Announce banner sits at 45% height.

summary: Tutorial step 2 ignores the guaranteed newbie car (TutorialForUserId is never read). It targets the nearest Parked car by straight-line distance from inside the garage, which on several plots is a car behind or beside the garage walls.
evidence: StreetSpawnService.luau:12-13 says the car is tagged 'for the tutorial arrow', and lines 427-430/443-450 set TutorialForUserId. A grep of src/client finds no reader. TutorialController.luau:931-940 collects every Kind=='Parked' model and calls pickNearest(candidates, root.Position) with no maxDistance. pickNearest (175-188) is pure Euclidean. OwnerSpawn is at local z=+24 (Map.luau:77) while the only door is at FRONT_Z=-44 (Map.luau:62; walls at PlotService.luau:401-405). Replaying MapLayout.parkingSpots(): the nearest spot to OwnerSpawn is behind or beside the garage on plot 4 (89 studs), plot 6 (81), plot 7 (56) and plot 8 (66). The curbside newbie car is about 94 studs away. Plot 1 has a back spot at 114. About 26 of 70 spots are filled at any time.
failureScenario: A new player on plot 7 spawns facing the door. The STEAL! beam and the AlwaysOnTop highlight point through the back wall at a car on the ring road. They walk into the wall and get no hint to go out the front. The arrow only switches to the curbside car once they happen to leave through the door, because retarget runs every 2s. This breaks SPEC §2 step 2 for roughly a third of new players on those plots.
suggestedFix: In retarget(), use the model whose TutorialForUserId equals LocalPlayer.UserId when it exists. Otherwise only consider cars in front of the door (same test as StreetSpawnService._inFrontOfDoor) and pass a maxDistance. While the root is inside MapLayout.plotInteriorZone(plotIndex), point the waypoint at the door (plotToWorld(idx, (0,0,FRONT_Z-6))) and keep the car highlight.
verifyReason: Confirmed. Nothing in src/client reads TutorialForUserId; StreetSpawnService sets it at lines 429/449 and the docs mention it, but no client code uses it. retarget() (TutorialController.luau:923-962) collects every Kind=='Parked' Vehicle and calls pickNearest(candidates, root.Position) with no maxDistance and no front-of-door filter. I replayed MapLayout.parkingSpots() (70 spots) against OWNER_SPAWN (local z=+24) and got the same numbers as the tracer. The nearest spot is behind or beside the walls on plot 4 (89.5), plot 6 (81.0), plot 7 (55.5) and plot 8 (66.0); the curbside newbie car is 94.1. Plot 1 also goes wrong when ensureNewbieCar reuses the existing front Common at 159.6 and the back spot (113.9) is filled. WaypointController draws a straight Beam and the Highlight is AlwaysOnTop, so both point through a solid wall (PlotService walls ~401-405, one door at FRONT_Z). The hysteresis (25 studs) makes it worse: once the wrong car is picked, a newbie car that spawns or tags later can't take over until the player is out the door. PlotService.assign hands out the lowest free plot, so plots 4-8 go to players joining busy servers. It is recoverable (the door is right in front of the spawn), but it is wrong on the critical first-60s path the SPEC calls out.
fix: src/client/Controllers/TutorialController.luau, retarget(): (1) First look for a Model tagged Vehicle with Kind=='Parked' and GetAttribute('TutorialForUserId')==player.UserId. If one exists, target it directly and skip the hysteresis block, so a newbie car tagged late still wins. (2) Otherwise, when plotIndex() is known, keep only candidates on the street side of the door. Use door = MapLayout.plotToWorld(idx, Vector3.new(0,0,MapConfig.Garage.FRONT_Z)).Position and face = MapLayout.plotOrigin(idx).LookVector (flattened), and accept (pos-door):Dot(face) > -4, the same test as StreetSpawnService._inFrontOfDoor. If that leaves nothing, fall back to the current all-cars list. Optional: while the root is inside MapLayout.plotInteriorZone(idx) and no tagged car exists, point the waypoint at plotToWorld(idx,(0,0,FRONT_Z-6)) labelled 'STREET' and keep the car highlight. No server change is needed.

summary: The dealership step is an 8-second timed card. The dealership waypoint is cleared when the tutorial ends, so the player is never actually guided to the Dealership or to upgrades.
evidence: STEPS[5] has timed = 8 (TutorialController.luau:94-101). transition() returns DONE after elapsed >= DEALER_SECONDS with no position check (164-167). enterStep sets the waypoint (987-991), then finish calls teardown, which runs setWaypoint(nil) (994-1001, 1003-1010). The step starts at the CollectPad at the back of the garage (Map.luau:73), hundreds of studs from the Dealership at block (0,0).
failureScenario: After collecting, the arrow appears for 8s, then the confetti card and the arrow disappears before the player has left the garage. TutorialDone has already been fired, so there is no follow-up objective. This misses SPEC §2.4 'Arrow → Dealership / upgrades' and leaves the new player with no next goal.
suggestedFix: Make step 5 complete on arrival: MapLayout.poiCenter('Dealership') within ~60 studs, or a 90s timeout. Keep the waypoint until then, and fire TutorialDone on arrival. Optionally add a 'GEAR SHOP' step toward MapLayout.gearShopCounter().
verifyReason: Confirmed. STEPS[5].timed=8 (lines 94-101). transition() returns DONE once elapsed>=DEALER_SECONDS with no position check (164-167). enterStep sets the Dealership waypoint (987-991), and finish() then teardown() calls setWaypoint(nil) (994-1010). The step starts at the CollectPad at the back of the garage (local z=40), or after the 20s collect timeout. Walking to the door alone takes about 5s at WalkSpeed 18, and the Dealership block is hundreds of studs away, so the arrow always disappears long before arrival. No other client code points at the Dealership afterwards (grep: only TutorialController uses poiCenter('Dealership')), and TutorialDone has already fired. SPEC §2.4 'Arrow → Dealership' is effectively not met. Medium rather than high because the obvious loop (steal more) still works without it.
fix: src/client/Controllers/TutorialController.luau: remove timed=8 from STEPS[5] (or replace it with a long timer) and add nearDealer:boolean to Ctx. In tick(), set nearDealer to whether the flat distance from rootPart() to MapLayout.poiCenter('Dealership') is <= ~70. Make transition(STEP_DEALER) return DONE when ctx.nearDealer or ctx.elapsed >= DEALER_TIMEOUT (~90). Keep the waypoint until then; TutorialDone still fires from finish(). Update tests/spec/hud.spec.luau:213, which asserts DEALER at elapsed=8 -> DONE, to cover nearDealer and the new timeout. A Gear Shop step is optional.

summary: 8s after a brand-new player loads, the server toasts 'Tap 📅 to claim' while the tutorial's focus mode is hiding every menu button, including 📅.
evidence: RewardsService.luau:760-767 runs task.delay(8) and notifies if getDailyView().canClaim. A new profile has lastClaimDay=0, so canClaim is always true. TutorialController.luau:965-971 calls setHudFocus(true) in steps 1-2 (focus lasts up to FOCUS_MAX_SECONDS=150, line 121). HUDController.luau:1381-1384 sets u.menu.Visible=false and u.topRow.Visible=false while focused.
failureScenario: During 'YOUR CAR MAKES MONEY!' or 'STEAL A CAR!' a toast tells the player to tap a button that doesn't exist. This splits attention in the critical first minute and clashes with SPEC §1.6 ('no reading required').
suggestedFix: In onLoaded, skip the daily nag when data.tutorialDone == false, and send it from the TutorialDone handler or when focus is released. Hold Hot Drop/event Announce banners for tutorial players the same way.
verifyReason: Confirmed. RewardsService.onLoaded runs task.delay(8) and notifies when getDailyView().canClaim is true (760-767). A new profile has daily.lastClaimDay=0, so it always fires. The tutorial starts at about snapshot-ready + 1.5s and step 1 lasts 4s, so the toast lands in step 1 or 2 while setHudFocus(true) has set u.menu.Visible=false (HUDController 1381-1384). The Daily button is in MENU, so it is hidden. NotificationController does not check the tutorial. The toast also says 'Tap 📅' but the button icon is 🎁 (HUDController.luau:103), so the instruction is wrong even outside the tutorial. This is a distraction, not a breakage, so low.
fix: src/server/Systems/RewardsService.luau onLoaded: inside the task.delay(8) callback, return early when data.tutorialDone ~= true. Once focus mode ends, the Daily button's badge (HUDController.luau:1199-1200, set from snap.daily.canClaim) already advertises the reward. Also change the text to 'Tap 🎁 to claim' to match the HUD icon. Holding Hot Drop/Announce banners back is optional and out of scope.

summary: If the player hops out during 'DRIVE IT HOME!', the tutorial drops back to 'STEAL A CAR!', points at a different Parked car and shows a 'HOLD E' keycap. The player's own claimed Loot car right beside them can only be re-entered with F ('Get in').
evidence: transition() returns STEP_STEAL after 2.5s out of the car (TutorialController.luau:156-159). retarget/validParked only accept Kind=='Parked' (918-920, 931-939). VehicleService gives the unoccupied claimed Loot car an EnterPrompt on KeyCode F (1203-1213, 1238-1250). Its 'Hotwire' prompt carries HideForUserId = claimer (1256-1272), which DealershipClient hides for the claimer (447-463).
failureScenario: The new player stops short of the garage and gets out, maybe to look around. The arrow sends them to another street car while their stolen car sits next to them. Pressing E on it does nothing because only F is offered. If they leave, the car despawns after 45s (ABANDON_DESPAWN).
suggestedFix: In STEP_STEAL, first look for a Vehicle with Kind=='Loot', OwnerUserId==me and DriverUserId==0 within ~150 studs. Target it with the label 'GET BACK IN' and a keycap of F, 👆 or Y.
verifyReason: Confirmed. transition(STEP_DELIVER) returns STEP_STEAL after notDrivingFor>=2.5 (156-159). retarget and validParked only consider Kind=='Parked', and the step-2 card shows the 'HOLD E' keycap. After exit, refreshManagedPrompts (VehicleService ~1220-1272) gives the claimer an EnterPrompt 'Get in' on F/ButtonY (OnlyUserId=claimer) and a Hotwire prompt with HideForUserId=claimer, which DealershipClient.applyAudience hides locally. So the tutorial points at another street car while the player's own loot car offers only F. Impact is mild: the 'Get in [F]' prompt is visible right next to them, and stealing another Common works and is free of heat. The 45s despawn only happens if no player is within NEAR_PLAYER_RADIUS=120, so it doesn't apply while they stay nearby. Low.
fix: src/client/Controllers/TutorialController.luau: in retarget() (STEP_STEAL), first look for a Vehicle Model with Kind=='Loot', OwnerUserId==player.UserId and DriverUserId==0 (or nil), within ~150 studs. If found, highlight it, set the waypoint label to 'GET IN', and switch the keycap glyph to F / 👆 / Y (gamepad) with no 'HOLD' caption. Otherwise keep the current Parked logic. Shortening DELIVER_GRACE is not needed.

summary: Feel/design: about 86% of street steals (Common and Uncommon) add 0 wanted stars, so most early steals involve no getaway at all. This undercuts pillar 1 ('Every steal is a getaway') and makes buying Common/Uncommon cars at the Dealership pointless.
evidence: Rarity.luau: Common has streetWeight 60 and wantedOnSteal 0 (lines 37, 40). Uncommon has streetWeight 26 and wantedOnSteal 0 (47, 50). Rare and above total about 14. StreetSpawnService.luau:254 adds only tier.wantedOnSteal. Dealer prices are $120-400 for Common and $1,000-2,400 for Uncommon (Cars.luau), for the same $/s the player can steal risk-free in 0.8-1.2s.
failureScenario: After the tutorial a new player fills slots 2-4 with free, risk-free Commons and Uncommons. No police show up, so the drive home is just an errand. The dealership the tutorial points them to sells the same cars for cash.
suggestedFix: Keep the free tutorial steal, then make Uncommon 1★ and give Common a 30-50% 'witness' 1★, with a gentle single cruiser and long bust time. Alternatively, a parked steal could set off a car alarm that summons one patrol unit for 15s.
verifyReason: The facts are right. Common has streetWeight 60 and Uncommon 26, both with wantedOnSteal 0, so about 86% of unboosted street rolls add no heat. StreetSpawnService.onStolen only adds tier.wantedOnSteal. Dealer Commons cost $120-400 and Uncommons $1000-2400. However, this matches the SPEC mechanism ('wanted stars rise with rarity', §2.5/§6), and carjacks (Heat.carjack=1), dealer steals, hot drops and player thefts all add heat. It is a tuning/design call against pillar 1 and RESEARCH ('every steal becomes a getaway'), not a code defect. Low, as a balance item.
fix: Tuning only, in src/shared/Config/Rarity.luau: set Uncommon.wantedOnSteal = 1. The first-ever steal is still exempt via VehicleService.addStealHeat/isFirstSteal, and WantedService halves heat for brand-new players. A 'witness' chance for Common needs new code in StreetSpawnService.onStolen, e.g. rng < 0.35 adds 1. Treat that as a design decision to playtest, not a bug fix.

summary: E is the key the tutorial teaches players to hold to hotwire, and it is also bound to EXIT while driving. Steal prompts on nearby parked cars stay visible while driving and invite that press.
evidence: VehicleClient.luau:716-726 binds ACTION_EXIT to F, E and ButtonA at High+50 with Sink. TutorialController.keyFor returns 'E' (206-213). Nothing hides Hotwire/Carjack prompts while the Driving attribute is true: EffectsController only rescales them (1534-1540), and GarageClient only touches DisplayCar prompts (119-150). The server rejects with 'You're already driving!'.
failureScenario: A newcomer driving past parked cars sees 'Hotwire [E]', presses E and is thrown out of the car mid-delivery. That sends the tutorial back to step 2 (see TUT-REGRESS-CLAIMED).
suggestedFix: Drop Enum.KeyCode.E from HC_Exit (keep F and the EXIT button). Locally disable steal-type prompts while player:GetAttribute('Driving') is true.
verifyReason: Confirmed. HC_Exit is bound to F, E and ButtonA at High+50, and pressHandler acts on Begin and Sinks (VehicleClient.luau:679-726). VehicleClient.exit() sets Humanoid.Jump, so a single E tap leaves the car. Steal prompts default to KeyCode E and MaxActivationDistance 12. A car in the travel lane (8 from centerline) passes parked cars (15.5) and adjacent-lane traffic within 12 studs, and nothing hides Hotwire/Carjack prompts while Driving: EffectsController and DealershipClient only rescale or filter them by audience, and GarageClient only touches DisplayCar prompts. Roblox does not hide ProximityPrompts for seated characters. The server would reject the steal anyway ('You're already driving!'), so the prompt is pure bait. During the tutorial this drops the player back to step 2.
fix: Minimal: remove Enum.KeyCode.E from the HC_Exit binding in src/client/Controllers/VehicleClient.luau:716-726. F, ButtonA and the touch EXIT button remain. Update the binding list in docs/integration/vehicles-world.md:14. Optionally also hide steal-type prompts (names Hotwire/Carjack/StealPrompt) locally while player:GetAttribute('Driving') is true. Do not toggle ProximityPromptService.Enabled globally, because CombatClient already owns that toggle for stuns.

summary: Exploitable: the garage display-car StealPrompt never clears a hold that was started and then aborted. An exploiter can pre-charge the hold timer and then trigger instantly.
evidence: GarageService.luau:552-563 records display.holds[p] on PromptButtonHoldBegan and only reads and clears it in Triggered. There is no PromptButtonHoldEnded handler. VehicleService.addStealPrompt does reset interrupted holds (VehicleService.luau:1061-1067).
failureScenario: The exploiter taps E on a victim's display car, which records 'began', and releases. They wait the required time, set HoldDuration=0 locally and press E. Triggered passes the os.clock()-began check, giving an instant steal from a player garage.
suggestedFix: Add steal.PromptButtonHoldEnded: if os.clock()-began is less than _requiredHold(base, holdMultiplier(p)), clear display.holds[p]. That mirrors VehicleService.
verifyReason: Confirmed. GarageService.luau:552-563 records display.holds[p] on PromptButtonHoldBegan, and only Triggered reads and clears it; there is no PromptButtonHoldEnded handler. VehicleService.addStealPrompt does clear interrupted holds (1061-1067). An exploiter can begin a hold, release, wait out _requiredHold, then trigger instantly. That bypasses the defender's chance to interrupt the hold (bat/zapper stun) and lets them pre-charge before a lock expires. beginTheft still enforces presence in the interior, the lock, newbie protection and cooldowns, so the gain is limited. Low. Minor related point: holds is a strong-keyed table that is never pruned on PlayerRemoving, but it dies with the display.
fix: src/server/Systems/GarageService.luau, after the PromptButtonHoldBegan connection, add: steal.PromptButtonHoldEnded:Connect(function(p) local began = display.holds[p]; if began and os.clock() - began < GarageService._requiredHold(base, holdMultiplier(p)) then display.holds[p] = nil end end). This mirrors VehicleService.

summary: Every spawn and respawn first places the character on the plaza SpawnLocation, then pivots it to the garage a deferred tick later. The player sees the plaza and a camera snap, and the server teleport races the engine's own spawn placement.
evidence: CharacterAutoLoads=true (default.project.json). The only SpawnLocation is at the plaza (MapBuilder.luau:1257-1271). PlotService.onCharacter uses task.defer then WaitForChild and moveCharacterHome (PlotService.luau:1456-1464).
failureScenario: A new player's first frame shows the plaza and the camera snaps into the garage, which breaks SPEC §2.1 'Spawn inside your own garage'. If the engine's spawn placement ever lands after the deferred pivot, the player stays at the plaza and the tutorial points across the city.
suggestedFix: Give each plot a non-Neutral SpawnLocation at OwnerSpawn and set player.RespawnLocation in assign() (clear it in release). Keep the pivot only as a fallback.
verifyReason: Partly confirmed. CharacterAutoLoads=true, and the only SpawnLocation is the Neutral plaza pad (MapBuilder.luau:1257-1271). PlotService.onCharacter runs task.defer, then WaitForChild('HumanoidRootPart'), then PivotTo (1456-1464). So every spawn places the character at the plaza first, and the client sees a snap once the server pivot replicates. On first join this is mostly hidden by loading; on respawn it is visible. The claim of a race where engine placement lands after the deferred pivot is speculative: LoadCharacter places the character before parenting, and the handlers are deferred twice. Cosmetic, low.
fix: src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau: build one SpawnLocation per plot at ownerSpawnCFrame(index). Make it Neutral=true, because teamless players can only use a neutral RespawnLocation, and CanTouch=false. Set player.RespawnLocation in assign() and clear it in release(). assign() runs in PlayerAdded before the character loads. Keep moveCharacterHome as the fallback, and keep the plaza pad in MapBuilder.luau for unassigned players. Verify in Studio that unassigned players don't randomly pick a plot spawn. If they do, set Enabled=false on plot spawns and confirm RespawnLocation still honours them.

summary: Returning-player edge cases. Tutorial progress isn't saved, so a player who disconnects before TutorialDone restarts at step 1 with menus hidden. If their garage is already full, 'DRIVE IT HOME!' can never complete.
evidence: begin() always runs goTo(STEP_MONEY) (TutorialController.luau:1156-1157). Step 3 only advances when garageCount or stealCount rises (143-145, 1079-1080). onDelivery with a full garage just toasts and returns without storing or counting a steal (GarageService.luau:1100-1110).
failureScenario: A player delivers several cars during steps 4-5 and leaves before the 8s dealer card fires TutorialDone. On rejoin, focus mode hides the menus again for up to 150s. With 4/4 slots they deliver into a 'Garage full!' loop and the card never advances unless they find SKIP.
suggestedFix: Fire TutorialDone, or persist a tutorialStep, as soon as the first delivery happens (stats.steals > 0). In shouldRun, skip the tutorial for profiles with stats.steals > 0.
verifyReason: Confirmed but narrow, and already documented as a known limitation (docs/integration/gameplay-client.md:345). begin() always starts at STEP_MONEY. Only tutorialDone is persisted, and only by finish() (DataService TutorialDone handler). A player who disconnects in the ~28s between first delivery and TutorialDone (collect timeout 20s + dealer 8s) restarts at step 1 with focus mode. The 'Garage full' deadlock is real in code: GarageService.luau:1100-1110 returns without counting a steal, and step 3 only advances on garageCount or stealCount rising. Reaching it, though, needs 3 extra cars (START_SLOTS=4) without the tutorial ever finishing, which is practically unreachable. SKIP and the 150s focus cap still work.
fix: src/client/Controllers/TutorialController.luau start(): after onReady, if snap.tutorialDone == false and TutorialController.stealCount(snap) > 0, call pcall(Net.fire, 'TutorialDone') and return without begin(). Optionally fold that into shouldRun(), and update the hud.spec shouldRun cases. stats.steals only increments on delivery, so this means 'already delivered once'.

summary: Feel: offline earnings are credited before the 'WHILE YOU WERE AWAY' modal appears. The COLLECT button is cosmetic, and the HUD cash counter has already jumped behind the dimmed modal.
evidence: RewardsService.luau:703-706 calls addCash (which sets the Cash attribute immediately) and then fires OfflineEarnings. In NotificationController.luau:1166-1178, COLLECT only closes the modal or plays the coin burst.
failureScenario: A returning player sees their cash already up by $7,560 behind the dim overlay. Pressing COLLECT then animates coins into a counter that doesn't change, so the payoff moment is lost.
suggestedFix: Have HUDController suppress or freeze the cash tween while the offline modal is open and count up when COLLECT is pressed. Or pay through a ClaimOffline remote with a server auto-claim after 30s.
verifyReason: Confirmed. grantOffline calls DataService.addCash, which sets the Cash attribute, and then fires OfflineEarnings (RewardsService.luau:703-706). NotificationController's COLLECT only calls closeOffline(true), which plays a coin burst, sounds and a fade. Auto-close does the same without the burst. The HUD counter has already moved behind the semi-transparent Dim before the player presses COLLECT. This is feel/polish only, with no economic effect. New players never see it (info.isNew returns early).
fix: Client-only, to keep the economy server-authoritative and unchanged: add NotificationController.isOfflineOpen() (or a signal) and have HUDController's Cash-attribute handler defer its counter tween while the modal is open. Call the HUD refresh from closeOffline() so the count-up plays with the coin burst. Files: src/client/Controllers/NotificationController.luau and src/client/Controllers/HUDController.luau. A server ClaimOffline remote is unnecessary.

summary: The tutorial's 'HOLD E' keycap stops pulsing as soon as step 2 starts. Kit.pop tweens the same UIScale that carries the infinite pulse tween, which cancels it.
evidence: keyScale is created with an infinite tween to Scale=0.9 (TutorialController.luau:715-716). renderStep calls Kit.pop(c.key, 1.4) when showKey is set (810-812). Kit.pop reuses FindFirstChildOfClass('UIScale') and tweens it to 1 (Kit.luau:373-377).
failureScenario: The one visual cue that teaches 'hold' sits static for the whole steal step.
suggestedFix: Pop a wrapper frame (or keyTop) instead of `key`, or restart the pulse tween after the pop completes.
verifyReason: Confirmed. keyScale is a UIScale under `key` with an infinite reversing tween to Scale 0.9 (TutorialController.luau:715-716). renderStep calls Kit.pop(c.key, 1.4) whenever the key is shown (810-812). Kit.pop reuses the existing UIScale (FindFirstChildOfClass) and plays a new Scale tween. TweenService cancels the earlier tween on the same property, so the pulse dies on the first render of step 2. The key is hidden during step 1, so the pulse is never seen.
fix: src/client/Controllers/TutorialController.luau buildCard(): move the pulse UIScale and its tween from `key` to `keyTop`, creating it after keyTop. Kit.pop(c.key, 1.4) then owns key's own UIScale, and the two nested scales multiply without cancelling each other. Alternatively, change line 811 to Kit.pop(c.keyLabel, 1.4).

summary: The first Rebirth request from each player is always silently dropped because the remote's rate limit is 0.5/s.
evidence: RebirthService.luau:303-305 registers `Net.on("Rebirth", ..., 0.5)`. Net.luau:100 creates the token bucket with `tokens = perSecond` (0.5), and Net.luau:105 `if b.tokens < 1 then return false`, so the first call is rejected with no feedback. MenuController.luau:2812-2817 sends a single `Net.fire("Rebirth")` after the confirm tap, then shows 'REBIRTHING...' for PENDING_SECONDS=3 (line 75). AdminService.luau:456 calls RebirthService.rebirth directly, so admin QA and the unit tests never go through the limiter.
failureScenario: A player saves up $750K, opens REBIRTH, taps twice to confirm, sees 'REBIRTHING...' for 3s, and then nothing happens. No Notify is sent and the button resets. They have to repeat the whole double-tap (at least 1s later) for it to work. The first press of the main retention action fails in every server session.
suggestedFix: Register the handler with a rate of at least 1 (for example `end, 1)`), since `busy[player]` already blocks concurrent rebirths. Alternatively, change `Net.allow` to start the bucket at `math.max(1, perSecond)` tokens.
verifyReason: Confirmed. CarBuilder.luau:159-160,547-565 places two collidable massless Balls (d=1, bottom 0.25) at x=0, z=axleF/axleR. Nothing in the repo turns them off: no CollisionGroups exist, and grep finds no BumpStop handling in PoliceService, VehicleService or VehicleController. The tracer's claim that 'the server does the same for police' is wrong, so police cars snag too. At rest the ball bottom is 0.25+RIDE_LIFT 0.2 = 0.45, below CURB_HEIGHT 0.6. Sidewalk strips are vertical-faced blocks (MapBuilder 1116-1210); only DrivewayRamp curb cuts are wedges. Suspension rays go straight down from the hub (VehicleController 613), so they only reach the curb top once the hub is over it. At curb height the ball reaches about 0.357 ahead of the axle, so it strikes the curb's top corner with a roughly 44° normal. Elasticity is 0. Downforce adds 0.002·v²/(4·68) of compression: about 0.07 at 100 studs/s, and about 0.38 at 227 (hypercar nitro), which leaves about 0.07 of clearance. These numbers match the tracer. With pitch inertia included, my estimate is about 22 studs/s of forward speed lost and 22 gained upward at 60 studs/s, a bit less than the claimed 30, but still a hard snag. Server crash damage (Δv>55) starts around 110 studs/s. The rear ball hits the curb again after the front wheels climb. The test at vehicle.spec 332-334 checks only the chassis bottom.
fix: Do not just raise BUMPSTOP_CLEARANCE. At 0.65 the ball still dips under 0.6 at speed (0.85-0.38), and cars resting without a controller sink 0.65 into the road. Instead, change src/shared/Vehicle/VehicleController.luau: in new(), for every model child named "BumpStop" that is a BasePart, store its CanCollide and set it false; restore it in destroy() (pcall, skip if the part is gone). On the driver's client this changes only the owner's local simulation, which is the one that counts for a client-owned assembly. On the server (police, and the F4 settle controller) it replicates harmlessly. While driving, the chassis box (bottom ≥0.95 with the lift) still keeps the car off the ground. In tests/spec/vehicle.spec.luau, add a check that BumpStops are CanCollide=false after VC.new and true again after destroy, and a note/assert that stop bottom + RIDE_LIFT < CURB_HEIGHT, which is why they must be disabled.

summary: Every gamepass and product id is 0 (and GROUP_ID is 0), so the Store, all pass effects and the group bonus are off at launch. Garage pads 11-12 also advertise a pass that can't be bought.
evidence: Monetization.luau:13/20/27/34/41 (passes) and 54/61/68/75/82/89 (products) are all `id = 0`. MonetizationService.luau:211 makes hasPass false for id 0. MenuController.luau:1510 `if items.comingSoon` renders 'STORE COMING SOON!'. GarageService.luau:138 sets `passOnly = not hasSlotsPass`, so pads 11-12 always show '🅿️ +2 SLOTS PASS' (GarageClient.luau:402), but the purchase prompt only appears when the pass id is non-zero (GarageClient.luau:457). Economy.luau:187 has `GROUP_ID = 0`.
failureScenario: At launch nobody can buy VIP, slots, Master Thief, Infinite Nitro, Zapper Pass, cash, Lockdown, Lose the Cops, Server Luck or the Dragster. The Store tab is a 'coming soon' card. Every player sees a gold '+2 SLOTS PASS' label on two pads that does nothing when they walk up to it.
suggestedFix: Create the passes and products on the Creator Dashboard and fill in the ids (plus GROUP_ID) as a release-checklist step. Add a server boot warning when any id is 0 in a non-Studio server. In GarageClient, only show the PassOnly label when `Monetization.Passes.slots.id ~= 0` (otherwise show a plain lock or hide the pads).
verifyReason: Confirmed. The Heartbeat at VehicleService 1739-1746 runs zonePass (every 0.2 s) before watchdogPass (every 0.5 s). zonePass (1460-1498) reads the live, client-replicated car.chassis.CFrame.Position and immediately calls fireDelivery, ChopAttempt or SprayAttempt. It does not compare against st.wdCFrame and does not check wdRevokedUntil. The handlers trust it fully. GarageService.onDelivery (1021+) checks no distance or time and destroys the car straight away for Loot/Owned. TheftService.complete (1223+) only checks thief/victim state. WantedService.onSprayAttempt (541+) only charges cash and clears the stars. Once the car is destroyed, the watchdog never samples the teleport, so a CFrame write from the owning client becomes an instant delivery, chop or wanted wipe.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau zonePass, before any zone action: skip the car if now < st.wdRevokedUntil. Then compute disp = flat(pos - st.wdCFrame.Position).Magnitude, dt = min(now - st.wdAt, WATCHDOG_MAX_DT) and hSpeed, and call VehicleService._watchdogVerdict(hSpeed, disp, dt, getSpeedCap(car)). If it returns a verdict, call violate(car, player, st, verdict, ...) and continue without firing any zone signal. Also move runPass('watchdog') above runPass('zone') in the Heartbeat. For extra safety, fire a zone only when the last watchdog-accepted position (st.wdCFrame.Position) is also inside it, which costs at most 0.5 s of delay. Add a vehicleservice.spec test: a car teleported into its drop-off does not fire DeliveryAttempt. Note that the remaining per-tick hop allowance is F5's problem.

summary: Stealing from the dealership costs a flat 2★ for any rarity, and spraying it off costs $500. A heist is worth about $40K on average, so Buy is pointless and early progression explodes.
evidence: DealershipService.luau:777 `addHeat(player, PoliceConfig.Heat.dealerSteal, ...)` with Police.luau:27 `dealerSteal = 2`. There is no rarity term (street steals use rarity.wantedOnSteal, up to 3★ for Mythic). Economy.luau:125 `SPRAY_COST_PER_STAR = 250`. Computed from Config/Cars + Rarity dealerWeight: expected car value per dealer roll is about $40K, so selling (50%) gives about $20K and chopping (35%) about $14K. 3% of rolls are Legendary+ (a Mythic chops for $525K-875K). A new player earns $3/s, so $40K is about 3.7 hours of income. A pad restocks 30s after a theft.
failureScenario: Within minutes of joining, players learn to rob the showroom over and over, chop or sell the cars, spray for $500, and reach rebirth ($750K) in a few heists. Buy prompts and car prices stop mattering as a cash sink, and the 'getaway' tension is gone because 2★ is trivial to lose.
suggestedFix: Base dealer-steal heat on rarity (for example `max(Heat.dealerSteal, tier.wantedOnSteal + 1)`, so Legendary+ is 4-5★). Scale the spray cost with income or with stars². Make dealer-stolen cars sell or chop for less (for example 15%, or no sell value for 10 minutes). Consider a per-player dealer-theft cooldown.
verifyReason: Confirmed. PlotService.pushOut (1229-1267) checks whether the intruder sits in a 'Vehicle'-tagged model and, if so, PivotTo's the whole car with the driver still seated onto the driveway at FRONT_Z-12-2. lockFor (1297-1310) calls pushOut immediately, and the heartbeat repeats it every PUSH_INTERVAL 0.5 s (1602-1619). TheftService checks the lock only in the start gate (336-337, 1034). This contradicts SPEC §6 line 106, which says only the character is pivoted out. While locked, the gate is CanCollide=true (applyLockVisual), so without this push a mid-theft lock would trap the thief inside. Instead the lock teleports the thief and the stolen car past the gate, and the victim's lock helps the attacker.
fix: In src/server/Systems/PlotService.luau pushOut, resolve the car with sys('VehicleService').fromModel(carModel). If car.kind == 'Stolen' (car.data.theft from this plot's owner), call VehicleService.eject(car) first. TheftService's DriverChanged→markDropped then leaves the car inside and gives the victim the Recover prompt. After the eject, pivot only the character to the driveway, as the else branch already does. For any other vehicle (the intruder's own Owned or Loot car), move it with VehicleService.teleport(car, cf), which pivots and calls resetWatchdog (this also fixes F7), instead of a raw carModel:PivotTo.

summary: Diamond Dragster is a repeatable Robux product worth $15K/s. It can't be stolen or sold and is never lost on rebirth, so stacking it is pay-to-win and breaks the rebirth curve.
evidence: Cars.luau:591-597 `diamond_dragster` has `income = 15000` (more than any Mythic at 4-6K/s), and line 604 has `stealable = false`. MonetizationService.luau:360-382 grants a new one on every purchase with no ownership cap. RebirthService.luau:104-108 keeps every Exclusive car through rebirth. GarageService.luau:860-863 blocks selling it. SPEC §9 promises honest, non-P2W monetization.
failureScenario: A player buys 4 Dragsters, earning $60K/s (×2 with VIP). Rebirth 1 ($750K) takes 6 seconds, R2 takes 25 seconds, and the cars survive every rebirth. Free players can't compete on the leaderboard, and other players have nothing to steal from them.
suggestedFix: Make it a one-per-account pass, or refuse the product when the player already owns one. Lower its income to around Epic or Legendary level (for example $1,500/s) or make it a cosmetic or speed car. Count at most one Exclusive among the cars kept on rebirth.
verifyReason: Confirmed. SPEC.md:115 and :261 call for a server settling controller, and the integration doc expects VehicleService to destroy it on sit. No such controller exists: VehicleController is created only by PoliceService (921) and the client. setDriver(nil) (841-853) only disables the seat and calls SetNetworkOwner(nil). Client-created movers never replicate, so once the server owns the car nothing holds it up, and it falls onto the two centreline balls. That support is unstable on a line, and the chassis COM is on the centreline because the other parts are Massless. CarBuilder's own doc admits a tilt of about 11°. The bigfoot chassis bottom is 2.7 (CarBuilder 1448), so its tilt is much larger. lifePass (1634-1645) then anchors the car in whatever pose it has. TrafficService.release (686-712) cleans up the Align movers with no replacement. One sub-claim is overstated: 'slides with no brake'. Ball friction 0.3, averaged with the road's, still stops the car quickly.
fix: Two fixes in src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau. (1) When a car loses its driver (the setDriver(nil) path), and also through a public VehicleService.settle(car) that TrafficService.release calls for rammed/knocked cars, create VehicleController.new(model, def, {isServer=true}) with zero input. Step it from one server RunService.PreSimulation loop over the settling set. Destroy it when lifePass anchors the car, when seat() or setDriver(player) gives the car a driver (before SetNetworkOwner(player)), and in destroy(). The client's _suppressForeignMovers already covers the replicated movers. (2) Before setting chassis.Anchored=true in lifePass, if the car is tilted (UpVector.Y < 0.98), PivotTo a level pose at RideHeight above a server ground raycast. Do not add hub balls (the tracer's option b): bull_charger and family_suv are already at the 40-part cap.

summary: Rebirth silently throws away all uncollected garage cash, and the Rebirth menu doesn't warn about it.
evidence: RebirthService.luau:258-266 calls `Garage.removeSlot(player, slot)` for every slot and ignores the returned record, which carries `uncollected`. Lines 267-268 then reset cash. The menu's 'YOU LOSE' list (MenuController.luau, Rebirth builder around 2760-2765) only mentions cash, cars and slots.
failureScenario: A player who returns after an hour has $500K+ sitting in slot billboards, rebirths straight away, and that money disappears without any notice.
suggestedFix: Before resetting, call `GarageService.collect(player)` (or sum the removed records' `uncollected` and add it to the player's cash before the reset, then show it in the toast). At minimum, add '💰 Uncollected garage cash' to the 'YOU LOSE' list.
verifyReason: Confirmed. _speedCap (386-392) is topSpeed×1.35×1.3×1.2 ≈ 2.1×topSpeed for every car. The spec test even locks this in, so a sustained 1.6× over the real nitro maximum passes; for a 130-top-speed car the cap is about 274. watchdogPass measures flat() displacement and horizontal speed only, so Y is never checked, while police bustPass requires |ΔY| < 10 (1781). The allowance accrues because wdAt only advances when disp > 0.01 or after 3 s (1576-1580), and dt = min(now-wdAt, 3). A car held still for about 2.9 s can therefore jump cap·2.9+10 in one tick: about 437 studs for a Rustbucket and about 1070 for a 175 car. The test 'lag stall: allowance accrues with dt' shows this was intended, but it can be exploited. Speed violations under 1.5×cap need two strikes. Part of the nitro choice is deliberate (every car has a nitro tank), but the vertical gap and the stall allowance are real holes.
fix: In src/server/Systems/VehicleService.luau and src/shared/Config/Vehicle.luau: (a) cut WATCHDOG_MAX_DT to about 1 s and update the 'lag stall' expectation in tests/spec/vehicleservice.spec.luau. (b) Add a vertical check on each watchdog tick: raycast down from the chassis (exclude Vehicles and characters); if there is no ground within about 40 studs for longer than about 4 s in a row (more than the MegaRamp's airtime), or upward displacement per tick exceeds a ramp-launch bound, call violate(). (c) Optionally take NITRO_SPEED_MULT out of the base cap and allow the nitro band only while a server-side budget lasts (the player's nitro-upgrade seconds plus NITRO_REFILL_PER_SEC, unlimited with the Infinite Nitro pass). Update the cap test to match. Do this together with F2.

summary: The Rebirth menu advertises '+10% rare car luck every rebirth', but REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS is never applied anywhere.
evidence: Economy.luau:120 defines `REBIRTH_LUCK_BONUS = 0.1`. MenuController.luau:2737 shows it as a rebirth benefit. A grep finds no server use.
